results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space, $S \subseteq E$, $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $p \in E$. results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Mean curvature under rescaling of the defining function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$, every $p \in E$ and every real $c \neq 0$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $c\rho$ through $p$ equals $c / |c|$ (the sign of $c$) times the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$.

results.title: Positive rescaling preserves the mean curvature
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$, every $p \in E$ and every real $c > 0$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $c\rho$ through $p$ equals the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$.

results.title: Reversing the normal negates the mean curvature
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and every $p \in E$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $-\rho$ through $p$ is the negative of the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$: replacing $\rho$ by $-\rho$ reverses the unit normal and changes the sign of the mean curvature.

results.title: Mean curvature of the unit sphere
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension $n$. For every $p \in E$ with $\|p\| = 1$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho(x) = \|x\|^2 - 1$ through $p$ is $n - 1$. That is, the unit sphere of $E$ has mean curvature $n - 1$ with respect to the outward normal, the mean curvature being the sum (not the average) of the principal curvatures.

results.title: Hyperplanes have zero mean curvature
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For all $a \in E$, $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $p \in E$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho(x) = \langle a, x \rangle - c$ through $p$ is $0$. In particular, for $a \neq 0$ the hyperplane $\{x \mid \langle a, x \rangle = c\}$ has mean curvature $0$ at each of its points.

results.title: Lattice cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $t, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \mathbb{N}^t$, the lattice cube with least corner $a$ and side $m$ is the set of points $x \in \mathbb{N}^t$ such that $a_i \le x_i < a_i + m$ for every coordinate $i$; it is a subcube of size $m^t$.

results.title: Membership in a lattice cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $t, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a, x \in \mathbb{N}^t$, the point $x$ lies in the lattice cube with least corner $a$ and side $m$ if and only if $a_i \le x_i < a_i + m$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Lattice cube of side one

results.title: Density one means containment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For sets $C, M \subseteq \mathbb{N}^t$, the set $C$ is $1$-dense in $M$ if and only if $M \subseteq C$.

results.title: Piecewise syndetic set

results.title: Gap size
results.caption: Definition

results.title: $(3+1)$-free posets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A partially ordered set $P$ is $(3+1)$-free when there are no elements $a, b, c, d \in P$ with $a < b < c$ such that $d$ is incomparable to each of $a$, $b$ and $c$ (neither $d \le x$ nor $x \le d$ for $x = a, b, c$).

results.title: Incomparability graph of a poset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The incomparability graph $\operatorname{inc}(P)$ of a partially ordered set $P$ is the simple graph on $P$ in which two distinct elements $x$ and $y$ are adjacent when they are incomparable, that is, neither $x \le y$ nor $y \le x$.

results.title: Chromatic symmetric function in as many variables as vertices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n = |V|$ elements, $X_G$ is the polynomial with integer coefficients in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ given by $X_G = \sum_{\kappa} \prod_{v \in V} x_{\kappa(v)}$, where $\kappa$ ranges over the proper colourings $\kappa : V \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ of $G$, that is, the maps with $\kappa(u) \ne \kappa(v)$ whenever $u$ and $v$ are adjacent.

results.title: $e$-positive polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A polynomial $f$ with integer coefficients in the $n$ variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ is $e$-positive when $f = \sum_{\lambda} c_\lambda e_\lambda$ for some natural numbers $c_\lambda$, where $\lambda = (\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k)$ ranges over the partitions of $n$ and $e_\lambda = e_{\lambda_1} \cdots e_{\lambda_k}$ is the product of the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_{\lambda_i}$ in $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$.

results.title: Statement of the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every finite $(3+1)$-free partially ordered set $P$, the chromatic symmetric function in $|P|$ variables of the incomparability graph of $P$ is $e$-positive.

results.title: Hikita's theorem: the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture holds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite $(3+1)$-free partially ordered set $P$, the chromatic symmetric function in $|P|$ variables of the incomparability graph of $P$ is $e$-positive.

results.title: Coverage of target depths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p, c, H$ be natural numbers with $p \le H$ and $c \le H$, and let $m = \max(p, c)$. Every natural number $j < H$ satisfies $j < p$, or $j = u + p$ for some natural number $u < H - m$, or $j = H - c + p + r$ for some natural number $r < c - p$, where $c - p$ is truncated subtraction (zero when $c \le p$).

results.title: Bounds on in-range and overflow target depths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p, c, H$ be natural numbers with $p \le H$ and $c \le H$, and let $m = \max(p, c)$. For every natural number $u < H - m$ we have $p \le u + p$, $u + p < H - c + p$ and $u + p < H$. For every natural number $r < c - p$, where $c - p$ is truncated subtraction, we have $H - m + p = H - c + p$ and $H - c + p + r < H$.
